text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- 1997 budget is presented to the cabinet today. The central government budget deficit is expected to reach 283.6 billion francs, while a deficit of 35 billion francs will be forecast for the separately run social security accounts. But the government will announce it expects to reduce the total public deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product, helped by a transfer of funds due from France Telecom. (Les Echos, Le Figaro).
-- Michelin tyre manufacturer posts higher profits for the first half, due to high tyre prices and cost-cutting, but lost its ranking as world's leader tyre maker to Japanese group Bridgestone.
-- Suez subsidiary Societe Generale de Belgique buys a further 24 percent share in Belgian electricity group Tractebel.
-- Alsace region and Strasbourg inhabitants refuse implantation of DHL express freight carrier's European hub in Strasbourg for environmental reasons.
-- Savings banks Caisses d'Epargne postpone project to bid for CIC bank.
-- Banques Populaires interested in taking control of Credit du Nord, a Paribas subsidiary.

-- Association of Credit Foncier minority shareholders start legal action against approval by bourse watchdog COB of bid on Credit Foncier planned by state-owned Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC).

-- French and German finance ministers meeting on Tuesday plan informal monetary stability council designed to support monetary stability pact to take effect when Europe shifts to single currency in 1999.
-- Union leaders Marc Blondel and Nicole Notat to compete for leadership of unemployment fund Unedic, which expects a 13 billion francs surplus this year.
-- Hard-line nationalists surge in Bosnia's election for three-man presidency.
